idea: External review proposal: replace fixed candidate windows (center ±1/±2s) with a step-wide search — coarse pass at 1-3s intervals over the whole step (frames extracted locally from the cached video, labelled with timestamps, sent in one request), then a fine pass at 4fps around the best hit. If the search finds nothing, none falls out naturally.
test_set: The 12 hardest guides from the 235-guide holdout: every guide where all three fixed-window candidates were unusable (Claude-graded). Includes all 4 confident-wrong-pick failures that three abstention attempts failed to fix.

borderline: #110 clip selected + cursor, drag not yet in motion
false_finds: #92 elbow crease (full-body long shot; the model's own rationale said 'not observed' yet returned found=true)

results.with_existing_verify_pass: Verify rejects #111 but passes #92 (the known long-shot blind spot). Net wrong photos on these 12: fixed windows 4 → adaptive 1 (+1 borderline). All 4 confident-pick failures resolved: 3 with genuine frames, #60 now a natural none.

cost.note: Request count is similar to today's pick+verify; the cost driver is tokens (~15x the selection stage). On request-limited free tier this is affordable; for token-billed keys it is the main tradeoff.

open_design_question: When to search. Escalating only when the cheap path answers none will NOT fix the confident-wrong picks (they never say none). Fixing those requires search as the primary candidate generator, which is the cost above and a 3-repo contract change (picker UI, candidate count, parity goldens). Decision deferred to the owner.
